saa-ini-061.text: During an unexpected peak of traffic, the application of a virtual store began to fail because the database did not support the volume of simultaneous writings coming directly from web servers. The architect suggested that the writings first go through a row, being consumed by the bank at the pace it supports.?
options: Row-based load leveling (queue-based load leveling), using buffer to absorb peaks
saa-ini-061.explanation: Putting a line between producers and the bank turns abrupt peaks into a constant flow that the consumer processes at his own pace — protecting the bank from overload and avoiding loss of requests.
saa-ini-061.hint: Think of the dam that holds the storm and releases the water in the flow that the turbine can handle.
optionRationales: Putting a line between producers and the bank turns abrupt peaks into a constant flow that the consumer processes at his own pace — protecting the bank from overload and avoiding loss of requests.
Accelerated cache LEITURAS repeated; the scenario gargalo is in the ESCRITAS Simultaneous caches that do not absorb.
Multi-AZ protects against zone failure, but the waiting replica does not increase the writing capacity — the peak would continue to overload the main.
Divide traffic by DNS between endpoints does not change the total volume of writing that reaches the same database.

saa-ini-062.text: Users from Asia and Europe complain of slow loading images and videos from a site hosted in the São Paulo Region. The architect wants to reduce this latency by storing copies of the content at points of presence near these users. What service solves the problem?
options: Increase the size of the instances EC2 in São Paulo
Amazon CloudFront, cache content in Edge Locations around the world
AWS Direct Connect for each international user
Amazon EBS with volumes provided on each continent
saa-ini-062.explanation: The CloudFront is the CDN of AWS: store copies of the content in hundreds of Edge Locations global, delivering it from the nearest point of each user and drastically reducing perceived latency.
saa-ini-062.hint: The problem is geographical distance; the solution is to bring the content of the user closer — what service does this?
optionRationales: The CloudFront is the CDN of AWS: store copies of the content in hundreds of Edge Locations global, delivering it from the nearest point of each user and drastically reducing perceived latency.
Volumes EBS are block disks attached to an AZ and instances — do not distribute content to global end users.
The Direct Connect is a dedicated physical link for companies to connect their data centers to AWS, inviable and meaningless to the general public of a website.
Larger instances do not decrease the physical distance between the server and users — the intercontinental network latency would continue to be the same.

saa-ini-063.text: A news site repeatedly consults the same set of headlines in the relational database to each access, overloading the bank and increasing the response time. The architect wants to save these results in an ultra-fast access memory layer, consulting the bank only when the data is not available in that layer.?
saa-ini-063.explanation: ElastiCache provides cache in managed memory: results of frequent consultations are served in microseconds of RAM, reducing the load in the seat and improving the response time of the application.
saa-ini-063.hint: Repeated consultations call for a 'short-term memory' between the application and the bank — what managed service does that role?
optionRationales: ElastiCache provides cache in managed memory: results of frequent consultations are served in microseconds of RAM, reducing the load in the seat and improving the response time of the application.
The S3 is durable storage of objects, with millisecond latency and no memory cache semantics for bank queries results.
The AWS Backup Centralizes Backup Backup — Does Not Accelerate Queries or Serves Real-time Data.
The Redshift is a data warehouse for mass analysis, not a layer of microsecond cache to relieve repetitive queries.

saa-ini-064.text: By creating a volume EBS for a common application (web server with moderate load), the architect seeks the type of volume SSD most recent general use, which offers good balance between price and performance and allows provisioning IOPS and throughput regardless of size. What type of volume meets this description?
saa-ini-064.explanation: The gp3 is the current generation of SSD for general use: delivery 3.000 IOPS and 125 Base MB/s regardless of size, with the possibility of providing more performance separately from capacity — better cost-benefit for common loads.
saa-ini-064.hint: Search for SSD 'generalist of the younger generation, whose acronym is "general purpose" to the number 3.
optionRationales: The gp3 is the current generation of SSD for general use: delivery 3.000 IOPS and 125 Base MB/s regardless of size, with the possibility of providing more performance separately from capacity — better cost-benefit for common loads.
Io2 is focused on critical databases that require tens of thousands of IOPS with maximum durability — performance and cost above what is required for a moderate web server.
St1 is an optimized magnetic disk for sequential throughput (big data, logs), inadequate as a general use volume with random I/O.
The sc1 is the HDD cheaper and colder, for rarely accessed data — the worst performance of the family, inappropriate for an active application.

saa-ini-065.text: A critical transactional database requires block storage with tens of thousands of IOPS consistent and the greater durability available in the family EBS. What type of volume was designed for this load?
saa-ini-065.explanation: The io2/io2 Block Express family is the IOPS provided by the EBS: consistent performance of up to hundreds of thousands of IOPS and superior durability (99,999%), designed for critical production databases.
saa-ini-065.hint: To IOPS extreme and guaranteed, search for the family whose name starts with the letter 'I/O'.
optionRationales: The io2/io2 Block Express family is the IOPS provided by the EBS: consistent performance of up to hundreds of thousands of IOPS and superior durability (99,999%), designed for critical production databases.
The gp3 responds well to general loads, but has a roof of IOPS much lower than the line of IOPS provided — insufficient for the requirement of tens of thousands of IOPS consistent.
The st1 is optimized for sequential reading of large blocks at low cost, with IOPS low — inadequate for intensive random I/O of transactional banks.
The Forum Store can be fast, but it is ephemeral: the data is lost with the instance stop, unacceptable for a critical bench without extra layers of protection.

saa-ini-066.text: An analytics platform continuously records large log files that are read sequentially in batches, prioritizing high throughput of reading at low cost, without need of IOPS What kind of volume? EBS offers the best cost-benefit for this pattern?
saa-ini-066.explanation: The st1 is the HDD optimized for throughput: ideal for intense sequential loads such as big data, log processing and home-made data warehouses, with cost per GB much lower than SSDs.
saa-ini-066.hint: Volumeful and cheap sequential reading combines with magnetic disk — which one is the 'optimized for throughput'?
optionRationales: The st1 is the HDD optimized for throughput: ideal for intense sequential loads such as big data, log processing and home-made data warehouses, with cost per GB much lower than SSDs.
Io2 is the most expensive option in the family, turned to IOPS Random guaranteed — waste for sequential log reading.
The gp3 would work, but the price of SSD by a sequential access pattern that a HDD optimized caters for much less.
The sc1 is for cold data rarely accessed; for continuous batch readings, its throughput base is lower than the st1.

saa-ini-067.text: Teams scattered around the world send large files daily to a single bucket S3 in the Oregon region, and the uploads from remote locations are slow. S3 speed up these shipments by routing them by Edge Locations of AWS?
saa-ini-067.explanation: Transfer Acceleration makes upload enter through Edge Location closer to the sender and follow the optimized backbone network of the AWS up to the bucket, significantly accelerating long-distance transfers.
saa-ini-067.hint: The trick is to get into the private highway of AWS by the nearest entry to the sender.
optionRationales: Transfer Acceleration makes upload enter through Edge Location closer to the sender and follow the optimized backbone network of the AWS up to the bucket, significantly accelerating long-distance transfers.
An Intelligent-Tiering Optimizes CUSTOS moving objects between access layers — does not change the speed of uploads.
A CRR copy objects to another region DEPOIS that reach the bucket — does not accelerate the path of the original upload.
Lifecycle administers transitions and expirations of objects over time, unrelated to transfer performance.

saa-ini-068.text: A system needs to send files from several gigabytes to S3. The team wants to divide each file into parts sent in parallel, with the possibility of retransmitting only the parts that fail, improving speed and reliability. S3 corresponds to this approach?
options: Compacting everything into one ZIP before sending
Upload via console in anonymous tab
saa-ini-068.explanation: The multipart upload divides large objects into separate parts sent in parallel; failures require only forwarding the affected part, being the recommended practice for files from 100 MB.
saa-ini-068.hint: The name of the technique describes exactly the method: send the object in 'multiple parts'.
optionRationales: The multipart upload divides large objects into separate parts sent in parallel; failures require only forwarding the affected part, being the recommended practice for files from 100 MB.
The browser mode does not influence the transfer mechanism — large uploads by the console remain subject to the same single flow limitations.
Compacting can reduce size, but keeps a single monolithic shipment: any failure forces you to restart from scratch.
Batch Operations performs mass actions on already stored objects (copy, label, restore) — is not the upload mechanism in parts.

saa-ini-069.text: An e-commerce uses Amazon RDS and realized that 90% of the operations in the bank are reading queries (product catalog). To scale the reading performance without touching the main instance, the architect added replicas that receive these queries.?
options: Replicas automatically replace the main one every hour to balance wear
Read Replicas receive asynchronous replication from the main and attend reading queries, distributing the load
The replicas accept readings and written simultaneously, doubling the total capacity
Replicas store only bank indexes, not data
saa-ini-069.explanation: Reading replicas are copies maintained by asynchronous replication that respond to reading queries, releasing the main instance for the writings — the standard path of reading scalability in the RDS.
saa-ini-069.hint: The name of the resource delivers its specialty: replicas dedicated to which type of operation?
optionRationales: Reading replicas are copies maintained by asynchronous replication that respond to reading queries, releasing the main instance for the writings — the standard path of reading scalability in the RDS.
Reading replicas do not accept writings (unless promoted); writings remain exclusive of the main instance.
There is no automatic roll of roles; the promotion of a replica is a deliberate action, usually in DR scenarios.
Replicas contain a complete copy of the data, kept in asynchronous synchrony with the main — not just indexes.

saa-ini-070.text: A mobile game uses DynamoDB it needs to reduce the latency of repetitive readings of milliseconds to microseconds placards, without rewriting the logic of the application (a) API of the DynamoDB What cache solution has been created specifically for this scenario??
options: Increase the reading capacity units (RCUs) of the table
Amazon CloudFront in front of the DynamoDB
saa-ini-070.explanation: The DAX is the cache in native memory and compatible with the API of the DynamoDB: Just point the client to the cluster DAX to obtain readings in microseconds, without changing the logic of the application.
saa-ini-070.hint: Look for the accelerator that speaks the language itself of DynamoDB.
optionRationales: The DAX is the cache in native memory and compatible with the API of the DynamoDB: Just point the client to the cluster DAX to obtain readings in microseconds, without changing the logic of the application.
The CloudFront makes web content cache (HTTP) on the edges — is not a bank call cache with compatibility of API of the DynamoDB.
DynamoDB does not have 'read replicas' like the RDS; its similar features (Global Tables) serve multi-region replication, not microsecond cache.
More RCUs increase the volume of supported readings, but latency continues in the house of milliseconds — it does not reach microseconds.

saa-ini-071.text: A startup will launch an application whose traffic is totally unpredictable — it can have tens or millions of requests per day. DynamoDB, which capacity mode avoids manual provisioning and collects only by readings and writings actually performed, climbing instantly?
options: Mode provided with low fixed values
Provisioned mode with high fixed values
saa-ini-071.explanation: On-demand mode, or DynamoDB adjusts the capacity instantly to real traffic and collects by request — ideal for unpredictable loads or new applications without history of use.
saa-ini-071.hint: Unforeseeable traffic combines with the mode that dispenses divination: pay for what happens.
optionRationales: On-demand mode, or DynamoDB adjusts the capacity instantly to real traffic and collects by request — ideal for unpredictable loads or new applications without history of use.
Providing for the peak would waste money in idle periods — exactly the problem that the mode on demand eliminates.
Low fixed capacity would cause throttling (rejected requirements) at unpredictable traffic peaks.
Reserved capacity presupposes stable and predictable long-term consumption — the opposite of the unknown traffic scenario.

saa-ini-072.text: A global application (not cacheable, based on TCP) suffer from inconsistent internet routes: users from some countries face high and variable latency to reach the endpoints of AWS. The architect wants to give the application two global static IP addresses and make the traffic enter the network of AWS by the nearest edge of each user. What service does this provide?
saa-ini-072.explanation: The Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs announced on the edges of the AWS: the user traffic enters the nearest Edge and travels through the private backbone of AWS to the endpoint, with lower latency and more consistent.
saa-ini-072.hint: Global static IPs + 'enter immediately the private network of AWS' = o global accelerator.
optionRationales: The Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs announced on the edges of the AWS: the user traffic enters the nearest Edge and travels through the private backbone of AWS to the endpoint, with lower latency and more consistent.
The CloudFront It's a CDN focused on content cache HTTP; for traffic TCP/UDP not cacheable with static IPs, the appropriate service is the Global Accelerator.
The simple route of DNS does not optimize the network path nor provides global IPs anycast — just solves the name for the same destination.
Elastic IPs are regional static addresses of individual fora — do not optimize the overall route of traffic through the network AWS.
